newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak parlt rejects direct presidential poll.
newsitem.headline: Slovak parlt rejects direct presidential poll.

text.p: Slovakia's parliament rejected on Wednesday an opposition proposal for direct presidential elections, with Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar's party claiming it could open a Pandora's box of popular votes.
The attempt to change the constitution so that the people and not parliament elect the president was defeated by 62 votes to 46 with 37 abstentions.

But opposition parties still hope to force a referendum on the issue. They have collected some 500,000 signatures on a petition urging President Michal Kovac to call a refendum on direct presidential elections.
Opponents of such a referendum say it could lead to further popular votes on subjects such as re-imposition of the death penalty.
"I can assure and warn you that a second or third referendum of this kind will approve the death penalty regardless of all legal and international barriers," Peter Brnak of the HZDS told parliament.

The governing coalition, led by HZDS, and the opposition appear unable to agree on a presidential candidate and neither commands the three-fifths majority needed to push through its own choice in a vote scheduled for March 1998.
In the event of such a stalemate, Meciar would assume presidential powers until a new parliament is elected in general elections planned for later in the year.
After Wednesday's vote, parliament began a special session to debate a bill, suspending bank priovatisation to the end of 2003, which Kovac returned to parliament for revision.
The government says the bill could jeopardise Slovakia's prospects of joining the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development.
